Activity 1.1: Provide agriculture and fishery inputs to framers and fishers (men and Women) with continuous technical extension support
1.1 Number of households receiving inputs to undertake farming and/or fishery. Disaggregated by gender
500 HHs (at least 52% women)
855 HHs supported (33% female-headed HH)

The original target was set conservatively to account for the high inflation and price volatility in Sudan. Through efficient procurement and cost management, the project was able to support more beneficiaries than initially planned without compromising the quality of assistance. This enabled inclusion of additional beneficiaries to ensure adequate representation of various ethnic groups in the target area as part of UNDP’s “Do no harm” principles.

Activity 1.2: Procure and deliver farm machinery, benefiting smallholder farmers with continuous technical follow-ups and support.
1.2 Number of male and Female smallholder farmers who have access to farm machinery to support food production
250 HHs (at least 52% women)

The machinery was allocated exclusively to Tokar following an assessment of land characteristics and local needs. The other target localities received support tailored to their contexts, including community farms, solar irrigation systems, and technical assistance. The CMC plans to expand mechanization services in the upcoming season to reach over 1,000 households in Tokar, which is within the seasonal service capacity of the two tractors. The expansion will be implemented by the CMC through its own operational guidelines, ensuring that services are extended beyond the original project beneficiaries.

Activity 1.5: Provide emergency employment focusing on young men and women through the construction and rehabilitation of critical community infrastructure.
1.5 Number of temporary emergency jobs created (for women and men)
392 HHs (at least 52% women)
1,007 HH heads (8.5% female and 81.5% male)

The project intentionally expanded beneficiary coverage in response to the high demand for emergency employment and the need to promote social cohesion among different ethnic groups, IDPs, returnees, and host communities. Efficient implementation also enabled the project to accommodate additional participants within the available budget.
Output 1: The food production (including crops, livestock, and fisheries) and income generation capacity of IDPs and Vulnerable Host Communities improved.

The types of work carried out mainly involved labor-intensive tasks, such as cleaning and rehabilitation activities, which were traditionally considered men’s work. Additionally, due to cultural norms in East Sudan, women are generally not permitted to work alongside men. However, IDPs were able to participate and benefit from these activities, allowing for some level of female inclusion despite these cultural constraints.
Output 2: Access of conflict affected IDPs and host communities to critical infrastructure and services enhanced
Activity 2.1: Establish and/or rehabilitate and solarize agricultural irrigation systems
2.1 Number of households benefiting from agricultural irrigation systems, rehabilitated/established, and solarized. Disaggregated by gender.
150 HHs (at least 35% female-headed households)
50 HHs (52% female and 48% male)

Demonstration plot supported 50 families (300 individuals). The demonstration plot will be used in a rotating basis with different households participating in different agricultural seasons. In the next season, a different set of 50 vulnerable families (300 individuals) will benefit from the farm to improve their livelihoods. Cumulatively, the farm will reach more than 150 HHs over time.
